os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Chrome headed under Xvfb 1280x800 (X11)
app: 16 live public websites in Chromium 148 (6 categories: vitrine, presse, commerce, media, reference, webapp, webapp-canvas) — Linux confirmation run of the macOS cell

stack_detection.method: open debug port answers /json/version; the sites themselves need no detection — the stack is the browser, not the page

channel_setup: This machine has no physical display, so the replication runs the FULL headed browser under Xvfb (xvfb-run + dbus-run-session; Xvfb extracted from .debs without root, one 8-byte binary patch to relocate its hardcoded /usr/bin/xkbcomp path) — NOT --headless, so the engine, UA and windowing path match the macOS methodology as closely as a server allows. Chromium 148 from the playwright cache, --remote-debugging-port=9223, viewport normalised to 1280x800 CSS via Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride{deviceScaleFactor:1}. Same script as macOS with only paths changed (campaign/linux/web-battery.mjs), same hardened distiller, same 16 URLs.

t1_read_text.detail: 16/16 sites yielded a readable structured view on the first try — including Amazon.fr and leboncoin, the two DataDome-guarded commerce sites that were the predicted casualties of a datacenter IP; neither raised a captcha. View latency 9-133 ms (mean 61 ms, median 60 ms) vs mean 16 ms on the macOS laptop — a slower shared server CPU, but still far below a screenshot round-trip.

t2_enumerate.detail: Interactive elements with boxes on every site. The occlusion-tagging profile reproduces the macOS layering signal: 4 on Hacker News (flat table layout), 9 on Wikipedia, 47 on Apple and YouTube home, 76 on BBC, 112 on Le Monde, 142 on YouTube watch — the last identical to macOS's 142. Same-day page churn moves individual counts but the flat-1990s-vs-layered-commercial ordering is intact.

t3_live_value.detail: Not exercised — no form filled on third-party sites (read-only discipline), same scope as the macOS cell.

t4_living_screen.detail: Not measured per-site; covered elsewhere (linux diff-streaming cell).

t5_blind_action.detail: Covered in depth by the companion cell linux-web-navigation-blind-cdp (8/8 on live sites, structured view only).

t6_pictorial.detail: Canvas/video sites all declared their opaque regions as '[pixels] x,y,w,h' lines: Excalidraw (canvas), Apple and Amazon (video), Stripe (canvas), YouTube home and watch (video). OpenStreetMap again declares tiled rather than one opaque canvas block. No site produced an EMPTY region where the screen shows content.

measurements.notes: THE MACOS COLLAPSE-TO-PARITY REPLICATES ON LINUX, NUMBER FOR NUMBER. Ratio of TOTALS: 1.00x (21946 structured tokens vs 16x1366 screenshot tokens; macOS: 0.98x). MEDIAN per-site ratio 1.15x (macOS: 1.15x, identical). Mean of ratios 1.28x (macOS 1.27x). Range 0.46x on Hacker News (identical to macOS's 0.46x) to 3.19x on Vercel (macOS: 3.11x). Structure wins on 10/16 sites — the SAME 10. By category: vitrine 2.20x (macOS 2.20x, identical), commerce 0.83x (identical), media 0.97x (identical), reference 0.96x (0.93x), presse 1.18x (1.21x), webapp 0.81x (0.78x), webapp-canvas 1.77x (1.74x). Avg screens to cover a full page: 7.6 (identical). The same 6 sites raised consent banners (Stripe, Vercel, YouTube home, BBC, Amazon.fr, leboncoin). This is the strongest possible form of the 'the ratio is a property of the PAGE, not the method' claim: two different OSes, different CPU architectures (x86_64 vs Apple Silicon), different Chromium major versions (148 vs 151), a real desktop session vs Xvfb on a headless server, two days apart — and every aggregate lands within noise of the macOS run, with several exact to the last digit. The only meaningful OS-level difference is capture latency (mean 61 ms vs 16 ms), which is CPU speed, not channel behaviour. Per-site deltas vs macOS are live-content churn (Amazon 2809 vs 3163 tokens: different result set for the same query; Le Monde 1769 vs different headlines), not distiller variance — the four static marketing pages land within a few tokens of their macOS values.

runtime_verification.method: Per-site viewport screenshot (PNG via Page.captureScreenshot) kept alongside the structured view; page-level counters (nText/nCanvas/nVideo/nImg/scrollH) read from the same DOM the distiller walked; aggregates cross-checked against the committed macOS run of the identical script.
runtime_verification.agreement: No site produced view content absent from the screen. Declared gaps are the honest ones: opaque media regions, occluded overlay-hidden nodes, off-viewport content dropped by design. Agreement with the macOS run is the headline (see notes): every category ratio within 0.03, three categories and the median exact.

permissions_required: None (loopback CDP socket; no root — Xvfb/xdotool extracted from .debs into a user-writable prefix). No account, no login, no cookie import on any of the 16 sites.
